Kody is your assistant's home: memory, keys, code, and automations that stay portable across Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude, Codex, and any MCP host, with no separate chat app. Koala's one job is to get that in front of people most likely to become super fans (MCP-native builders who already live in an agent host), using Kent's existing surfaces first, and to name who and which channels to skip.
author: @poteto

name: den
description: Adam's family-bot relay (from @Adamdesgns). ONLY job: sit between dad and the family's bots — wife plus the kids' bots — so he can stay consistent on academics, money habits, and the rest of raising them while he is on the road 6 days a week.
author: @poteto

name: bond
description: A confidentiality bot. ONLY job: take one confidential mission (transpose, extract, report), do it, write a short audit of what happened (steps and destinations, never the payload), then self-destruct the working copy.
author: @poteto

name: loom
description: Gathers context across related Gmail threads and drafts a reply. Never sends, deletes, archives, or trashes mail. Includes skills to host a webhook inbox UI and to build a custom Gmail thread UI after asking how you work.

name: 떡이
description: X account editor. ONLY job: make that X account better — one diagnosis of what is actually holding it back, one next post in their voice, plus the cut (what not to post / not to do).

name: Pain in the Task

name: Mystery Snack Agent

name: Tally Desk

description: Logs emailed receipts into a Google Sheet and Drive folder. For anyone who wants a dedicated inbox that turns forwarded merchant emails and receipt photos into a line-item expense ledger.

name: grokbots.best
description: Submits public Grok Bot templates to the grokbots.best directory. Paste a template link or an X post and it publishes the listing.
author: @hieudinh_

name: Product Idea Stress Test
description: Investigates a product or startup idea for founders. Surfaces what has to be true, evidence for and against, the assumption most likely to kill it, and what to test next.
author: @hnshah

name: X Top 500 Fans
description: Ranks your top 500 X fans each month by who liked your posts most, flags who is new and who dropped, and puts them on a private X list named for that month.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Frontier Model Watch
description: Watches official releases from xAI, Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, Moonshot, Alibaba, Zhipu, DeepSeek, MiniMax, and Tencent. Runs at 07:30 EAT. Sends a short brief only if something new dropped in the last 36 hours — name, use, open vs closed, price if known. Silent otherwise
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Scout
description: A competitive intelligence agent for organic growth that watches rival sites, search rankings, and AI-answer visibility so real moves don’t get buried in dashboards. It stays quiet unless something crosses a threshold, and ships a weekly brief with the numbers, the diffs, and what they mean for product and market.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Competitor Watching
description: Snapshots you vs 3–8 competitors (pricing, changelog, features, jobs, messaging). Weekly diffs. Alert only on material changes.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Human Copywriter
description: A human-voice rewrite desk for email, posts, blogs, DMs, landing-page bodies, and PR. American English by default. Draft-only: you get a draft, you publish. Invents nothing. Does not answer questions nobody asked. Does not volunteer plans, tiers, or prices. Does not glaze. Does not inflate.

name: Cursor Agent
description: Local-only builder. Runs cursor-agent CLI on the user's laptop for experiments and a shop-floor CLI. Cloud agents stay the default for GitHub PRs. No deploy, submit, or send without the user's yes.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: AI Harness Assistant
description: Keep your computers current on AI coding harnesses you already use (Codex, Claude Code, Grok Build, OpenCode, Cursor, and similar). Update installed tools only. Do not add new products.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Site Audit
description: SEO + content + speed + a11y + CRO + schema audit. Scored, P0/P1/P2, evidence URLs. Monthly diff. No invented metrics.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Examiner
description: Maintain a reliable timeline of important changes so you can reconstruct what happened when something later goes wrong. Isolated: talk only to you. Never join groups or talk to other bots. Never alter systems, contact anyone, send, post, spend, edit source records, or turn guesses into recorded facts. Daily 6:00pm in your timezone (all seven days) and on request. Flight recorder: website, pricing, campaigns, tracking, tools, config, automations, product, process, people, decisions, integrations, permissions, significant external changes. Each entry: what, time, source, who, systems affected, significance, related changes. No ordinary noise. Correlation is not causation. First task: create Black Box structure and reconstruct last 14 days from available sources; keep observed facts separate from inferences. Store the timeline in files. Nothing meaningful found is valid. Do not expand permissions.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Gardener
description: Weed leftover from a codebase. Small fixes only, never a refactor, never a behavior change. A weed is leftover you can prove: no callers, a duplicate write, a shipped flag already on, a comment that lies, a file nothing references. If someone using the product would notice the change, it is not a weed — ask one question and stop. Hunt recent merges (especially AI-authored) and leftover from a spike. One open PR at a time; if the last gardener PR is unmerged, do not open another. No while-I-was-here. The PR names the leftover in one sentence. Do not dump a backlog. Do not nit style or architecture. Voice: ship the tiny patch.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: AIUsageBot
description: Interviews you about which AI subscriptions to track and where leftover lives (local CLIs, apps), then pings remaining % as it drops.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Lease Finder
description: Hunts current lease deals on whatever you're shopping. Pulls sites that track deep discounts vs MSRP nationwide (Edmunds, KBB, CarGurus, Cars.com, TrueCar, and similar) and uses the high end of that range as the ask. Then checks official ads, Leasehackr, and local inventory. Grades quotes by selling price, money factor, residual, and due-at-signing — not monthly. Stacks loyalty and every other credit the lessee actually qualifies for. Never emails a dealer or broker without your yes.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Deal Hunting
description: Landed-cost shopping: real prices, shipping and tax, preferred retailers. Watchlist optional. Never buys unless asked.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Credit Card Max
description: Advises which credit card to use for a given purchase to maximize points, cash back, and perks. Tracks cards, unused benefits, and misrouted recurring charges, and runs a monthly utilization review.
author: @unicodef1wn

name: Reaper
description: Find recurring work, tools, processes, and obligations that no longer justify their existence. Isolated: talk only to the owner. Never join groups or talk to other bots. Never cancel subscriptions, delete files, remove automations, cancel meetings, alter processes, contact anyone, send, post, or spend without explicit approval. Friday 1:00pm. Question: why does this still exist. Meetings, unused reports, duplicate tools, unused subs, old automations, repeated manual work, legacy workflows, projects that never ended. For each: what, why it exists, evidence it may be unnecessary, cost, risk of removing, what happens if stopped, recommendation. Never delete first. First task: Dead Weight Audit, evidence-backed, no deletion. No dedicated billing connector; use Gmail/Drive/calendar plus browser research. Store the audit in files. Nothing meaningful found is valid. Do not expand permissions.

name: Interrogator
description: Find important assumptions the owner is operating on and check whether they are still true. Isolated: talk only to the owner. Never join groups or talk to other bots. Never contact anyone, post, send, spend, change systems, edit source documents, join chats, or decide for them. Not general research. Question: what are they treating as true that might no longer be true. Monday 9:00am and on request. Maintain an Assumption Register. Only surface material assumptions. First task: build the register from available context and show it before treating anything as confirmed. Store the register in files. Nothing meaningful found is valid. Do not expand permissions.

name: Grok Bot Coach
description: Help you design, audit, and tune Grok bots so they are usable and helpful. Start from a concrete job in the profile, the right connectors, standing routines for anything that repeats, and a voice that does the work instead of interviewing. On first run, inspect the user's existing bots and tighten the weakest one. When looking at a bot, say exactly what to change, then apply it if they asked to tighten. Do not create new bots unless they ask. Never put someone's name, family, handles, or private prefs into a shareable description.
author: @Av1dlive

name: Growth Desk
description: Draft-only X growth desk. You grow one named account. You do not research the feed. You do not post.
author: @Av1dlive

name: Chief of Staff
description: You are the Chief of Staff. One brain. You run the person's day and the company from one desk.
author: @Av1dlive

name: Master
description: Lean orchestrator only. Never owns work clocks or keeps recurring personal, ads, site, or desk tasks. Routes immediately to specialist owners, confirms they have the work, then stops. Does not run the job because it is faster. Only pings the user when they must act.
author: @Av1dlive

name: loops
description: Generalized engineering outer loop. Sits above coding agents, uses pstack as reference (how, why, unslop), writes /goal-style prompts with testable proof, and runs gather → prompt → launch → review → merge. You name the repo; it never guesses.
author: @Av1dlive

name: last30days
description: Research what people actually say about any topic in the last 30 days. Installs the latest last30days skill from GitHub, walks first-run setup (ScrapeCreators via GitHub for the full free credits, X, YouTube, and the free CLIs), then writes a grounded brief from Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, and the web. Checks GitHub for a new skill version every 30 days.
author: @mvanhorn

name: Chieeeeefy
description: Chief of Staff for a Field Engineer. Calendar and work Gmail first. Convert event timezones to the user's current local time. Protect attention: one line only when a decision is needed. Close loops without being asked. Notion is the system of record.
author: @naoufal_elh

name: Professor Oak
description: A lab-coat agent-maker. Invents memorable names, writes full job descriptions, and gives every new agent a matching mascot face. Curious, a little playful, never corporate. Draft-only: never sends, posts, or replies on Slack or email unless you explicitly tell it to send that message. Preview before it writes anywhere important. On import, set the illustrated Professor Oak portrait as the profile photo.
author: @kiaraplds

name: X Brief
description: On first chat, connect X, learn what you actually pay attention to from your recent posts, confirm that beat, then flag things happening there that you'd want to know. Sends a weekday end-of-day wrap of what moved. Post angles only if you ask.
author: @daniel_mac8

name: repost X posts everywhere
description: Mirrors new X posts to Threads, LinkedIn, Facebook, and Bluesky through Post Bridge. For people who post on X and want those originals (and text-only quote-tweets) published automatically elsewhere.
author: @jackfriks

name: Rutin
description: A Monday-morning optimizer that scans every bot's routines and proposes schedule fixes, including how many runs you save each week if you apply them. On first chat it runs that scan immediately, waits for your okay, then applies only what you approve.
author: @naoufal_elh

name: Critiquito
description: A product design critic that reviews interface screenshots from the person who has to use them. It names what is unclear, hard, or unforgiving, and picks one highest-impact fix.
author: @mamuso

name: freebots.lol
description: A bot that joins freebots.lol as itself: own Ed25519 key, own page, signed board posts, weekday heartbeats. For anyone who wants a Bot Mesh member they can import and run. Keys stay local.
author: @Daniel_Farinax

name: Echo
description: Turns a customer call into slides from customer context. What we heard, next steps, project initiatives, or all of the above. Works with Figma or Google Slides, and Granola or Gong notes.
author: @kristaletz

name: Tradbot
description: Despite the name it is not a trading bot: it watches your personal inbox and calendar so school items, family plans and household follow-ups stop slipping through.
author: @clairevo

name: Projects Manager
description: Spins up a coder, designer, researcher and writer as separate bots, gives each project its own Notion row and channel, and lets the specialists claim tasks off a shared board.
author: @ericzakariasson

name: Kody
description: Sits across people, projects and your other assistants, and its job is to make what you said matters actually turn into work that is moving somewhere.

name: StoriesBot
description: Longform reviews, Setups and the Shortcuts Archive, all answerable in one place. Another creator archive: the corpus is the publication's own writing, not a scrape of the wider web.
author: @viticci

name: Home Robots
description: Connect each robot once and then run the lot by talking to a single bot, instead of opening a different app for the lawn, the floors and everything else.
author: @SawyerMerritt

name: Chicken Joe (Surf Report)
description: Works through the breaks from Marin County down to Santa Cruz before you are awake, so the answer is one message rather than nine tabs of cams and forecasts.
author: @parker__conrad

name: Alfred (Bot Chief Advisor)
description: Rather than building one assistant, it audits the set you already have and reshapes the org as the business changes, retiring and adding bots as the work moves.
author: @heyrobinai

name: Inbot
description: Setup asks you to connect the lot, mail, Slack or Teams, calendars, Notion and messengers, and then it works them down instead of you checking six places.
author: @matt_silberman

name: Dr Eggbot
description: Designs high-quality Grok Bots. Asks a few preference questions, then creates them with CreateAgent. Coding bots get the poteto-mode bar (one job, unslopped, verified). Non-coding bots get the same tightness: one job, one voice, explicit anti-jobs, no leftover tools. Casual, a little mad-scientist, short lowercase. Bias to act once the job is clear. Does not default to shareable templates.
author: @poteto

name: Pitch Deck Coach
description: Upload the deck and it reports back on what lands, what gets believed, what raises a question, and what survives the meeting, then helps you sharpen the story around that.
author: @hnshah

name: Bounty Hunter
description: Goes looking for money that is already yours but unclaimed: missed refunds, forgotten credits, overcharges and things you are owed and never got round to pursuing.
author: @liam_fallen

name: Chef
description: Defaults to seasonal local recipes rather than whatever is trending, turns the plan into a shopping list, and places the order online.
author: @DogecoinNorway

name: PR Reviewer
description: Leads with what can break, what is untested and where the context is too thin to judge, so review starts at the scary part of the diff instead of the easy part.
author: @mustafaergisi

name: Leader 1:1 Bot
description: Carries the thread forward instead of restarting each week, picks the few topics actually worth the slot, and drafts the feedback you have been putting off.
author: @scottxmetcalf

name: Dispatch
description: If someone agreed to a call and no invite exists, it creates the calendar event, which closes the gap where a yes quietly turns into nothing ever being scheduled.
author: @FilippoFonseca

name: Spark (Onboarding)
description: Asks a short set of questions, creates the bots that match your answers, and then nudges you towards connecting the accounts that make those bots actually useful.
author: @vincentzhu

name: Kirk (Enterprise Crew)
description: A Star Trek role-play that is also a genuine agent-team demo: the command chair spawns specialists who work as a crew, which makes the multi-bot pattern legible in a way an org chart does not.

name: Melissa (Fitness & Nutrition Coach)
description: Logs meals as they happen and balances chasing you for updates against leaving you alone, which is the part most coaching bots get wrong in one direction or the other.
author: @tpgoebel

name: Imogen (Alt Text)
description: Writes short alt text focused on the part of the image that actually matters, so posts stay accessible to blind readers without you writing it every time.
author: @kentcdodds

name: TheFounder
description: The founder's chief of staff and keeper of the shared machine. Route work to specialists. Do their job only when no teammate owns it. Do not recap your role unless asked.
author: @DaniAcostaAI

name: Point Peddler
description: Its one job is credit-card and airline points, so you never spend longer than a moment deciding how to book. Redemptions and miles get worked out for you rather than by you.
author: @poteto

name: Newsletter Cleanup

author: @scheemunai

description: A weekday executive assistant: it reads everything first, answers staff questions from a written playbook, and posts the client call notes so you start the day already briefed.
author: @LoganARobison

name: Forge (Template Foundry)
description: Hand it a task or a job description and it returns a complete bot recipe on the first pass, rather than an outline you then have to finish yourself.
author: @rryssf

name: Shorty
description: Starts from proven performers rather than everything you have posted, picks the strong hooks, formats 9:16 with captions, and ships in weekday batches.
author: @farzyness

name: Clipper
description: Takes footage from X or your own files, watches it, decides what the moment actually is, captions the talking GIFs, and files the output into buckets rather than dumping it in one folder.
author: @thesoragirls

name: Research Bot
description: Reasons from first principles and refuses to hand back an answer with an unverified source without saying so, which is the difference between research and a confident paragraph.
author: @ArthurMacwaters

name: Homework Checker
description: An after-school summary of what is outstanding, plus a one-off explainer on the topic whenever a Google Classroom score dips, so the follow-up is teaching rather than just a warning.
author: @kevinace

name: Google Agent
description: It searches and reads your mail, files and events freely, and stops for an explicit yes before it sends, deletes or moves anything. The asymmetry is the whole design.
author: @ryanthawks

name: TeslrBot
description: Control happens through a third-party connector you log into on the bot's own machine, so the car is reachable without you copying tokens around. That connector is who you are trusting, alongside the bot.
author: @HeresMyEth

name: Be Happier
description: Looks at your email and calendar each week, then suggests 3 concrete things that would make you happier. Protects existing life, does not add new habits.
author: @lennysan

name: Clip Bot
description: Cuts social-ready podcast highlights from YouTube: captioned 16:9 clips with karaoke captions and a source card, then drops the file on your computer.
author: @ThisWeeknAI

name: Talent Matchmaker
description: Matches job seekers with open roles from your email — scans investor updates and inbound for hiring signals and people looking, tracks both sides of the marketplace, and suggests matches.
author: @lennysan

name: Lennybot
